Lemma
[$L^1$-norm of the Dirichlet heat kernel] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0360, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0361, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0362 ↗ lem:chow-iii-dirichlet-heat-adjoint-symmetry 1. ch26:26.10\group Dirichlet Heat Kernels

For an interior point $y$, \[ \int _{\mathcal M}H_D(x,\tau ;y,v)\, d\mu _{g(\tau )}(x) \le e^{C_1(\tau -v)}. \] There is also a constant $C<\infty $, depending only on the uniform metric evolution, curvature, injectivity, and boundary-distance data specified in the source, such that \[ \int _{\mathcal M}H_D(x,\tau ;y,v)\, d\mu _{g(\tau )}(x) \ge 1-C(\tau -v). \]
Proof

\sketch The outward normal derivative of the positive Dirichlet kernel is nonpositive, giving the upper differential inequality. For the lower bound, integrate against a time-dependent cutoff supported away from the boundary; uniform bounds for its time derivative and Laplacian yield the result.

□
